speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have experienced occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings since your tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly where you feel this pain and if it radiates anywhere?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent Cholesteatoma (post-tympanoplasty failure)

The combination of new-onset shooting pain triggered by swallowing (indicating Eustachian tube dysfunction or mastoid involvement) and tenderness to pressure on the ear canal suggests a recurrence of cholesteatoma or granulation tissue. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Temporal_Bone_right. REQUEST TEST: Microscopic Examination_of_Ear_Canal.
